items.title: In the quasi-coherent situation of a ringed site there is a cardinal kappa bounding the size of a nonzero map to any nonzero object and of a factorisation through a direct sum
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter sites-cohomology.tex (Cohomology on Sites)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file sites-cohomology.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma produces a single cardinal kappa controlling two approximation properties in the quasi-coherent category QC(O) of a ringed site: every nonzero object receives a nonzero map from an object of size <= kappa, and every map out of a small object into a direct sum factors through small summands (statement lines 11295-11309). Its non-formal content is the inductive claim (proof lines 11352-11429): one enlarges a subcomplex S_n inside a fixed representative F to S_{n+1} so that the kernel and image conditions hold for every morphism U -> V, choosing the required pieces by the More on Algebra enlarging lemma and realising them jointly by lemma-build-from, all while keeping size <= kappa, and then takes the union and uses that filtered colimits commute with the derived tensor product and cohomology. H2: one careful transfinite-free induction with two constructions, fully written out.
